A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DPA research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite the revised title and substantial relocation of experimental displays.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack-success experiments on LFW and CelebA-HQ, including robust victim models, JPEG compression, ablations, and supplementary visual-quality results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments in its main text and appendix, including attack-success tables, hyperparameter studies, and LPIPS results.

M1.justification: DPA retains the same DPO initialization, checkpoint selection, and HMA perturbation procedures in Algorithms 1–2. The input-transformation block added to Figure 3 was already present in v1's equations and algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions train parameter augmentation on BUPT-Balancedface and evaluate on LFW and CelebA-HQ. The existing JPEG-compression and robust-victim scenarios remain; the additional appendix sections relocate existing evaluations.

E2.justification: The eight principal baselines, separate LGV comparison, BSR comparison across victim models, and ablation comparators are retained in corresponding experiments. Adding a source citation for FIM does not introduce a new evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation settings remain unchanged, including the L-infinity perturbation bound of 10, 200 attack iterations, FAR@0.001 thresholds, model configurations, and appendix hyperparameters. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The stage ablations, intermediate-versus-final checkpoint comparison, JPEG robustness study, and visual-quality analysis are retained. The c and eta sensitivity studies move from v1 Section 4.3 to v2 Section 7.5 without changing the analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing averages across victim models and the plots' uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All eleven tables retain their numerical results after matching experiments, and the plotted findings are unchanged. For example, MobileFace-to-IR152/IRSE50/FaceNet ASRs remain 67.7/98.2/90.8% in v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 1. The isolated 5-to-5.0 edit is equivalent formatting.

T1.justification: The attack objective moves from v1 appendix Equation 18 to v2 Equation 1. Renaming the cosine-similarity matrix from m to r and clarifying notation preserve the mathematics. No substantive definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution bullets retain the same novelty and transferability claims. The expanded conclusion reiterates the existing mixed-initialization perspective and evidence across datasets and models.

C2.justification: v2 Section 4.2 newly attributes LGV's weak performance to instability caused by randomly selecting one model per iteration. v1 reports the comparison without this causal explanation. No additional experiment tests that attribution.

D1.justification: v2 Section 4.2 newly states LGV's one-random-model-per-iteration selection rule, adding limited comparator procedure detail. The DPA optimizer, learning rate, layer choices, hyperparameters, and resource-access disclosures remain unchanged; this does not establish a changed experimental setting.

R1.justification: Twelve references are added, covering FIM's source, data-free black-box attacks, deepfakes, and face anti-spoofing. These expand background and attribution while preserving DPA's central positioning relative to existing parameter- and feature-augmentation attacks.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include the title, affiliations, local explanatory and notation edits, an expanded conclusion, and acknowledgment and ethics sections. The optimization objective moves into the main text and the hyperparameter discussion into the appendix.

P2.justification: The experimental displays are substantially reorganized: three LFW comparison tables and Figure 7 move into the appendix, leaving one principal LFW table in the main text. Figure 2 corrects the backbone initialization colors, Figure 3 adds the existing input transformation, and comparison tables gain baseline citations.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity by correcting Figure 2's swapped initialization colors, showing the existing input transformation in Figure 3, placing the attack objective in Section 3.1, and improving baseline attribution. These are useful but limited gains: the scientific evidence is unchanged, and the added causal explanation of LGV's performance receives no new experimental support.
